about: How the ChatGPT/Codex package differs from the repo skills. The /chatgpt endpoint serves only the tools in chatgpt-tools.json: no Blender or Adobe bridges, no ask_mira, no trends, no raw uploads (chat attachments arrive through the client). The package is English only: `stripCyrillicTriggers` drops the quoted non-English trigger phrases from every shipped SKILL.md description, and rewrites cover the rest. Every `find` must match the source exactly once, so the build fails as soon as a source edit makes a rewrite stale. `override` files replace a source file whole; `sha256` is the source they were written against, and check.mjs fails when the source moves on without them. Tools in chatgpt-tools.json `renamed` are renamed in every shipped file: the bare lowercase word only (not Miracle, not miracle_*, not file names such as miracle.md, and not the `estimate_cost` kind value, which keeps its name).

rewrite.find:
When the user asks for a rough cut, you can start one: `film_edit_create` with the takes in order (videos
and stills butt-joined on the main track, audio on the music track), then `film_edit_update` with
`appendAssetIds` to add more. `film_edit_list` and `film_edit_get` read the team's cuts, `film_edit_render`
exports one to MP4 on Mira's servers for free, and `film_edit_export` gives a 30-minute download link for
editors outside Mira: `package` (every file plus XML, EDL and SRT), `xmeml` (Premiere Pro and DaVinci
Resolve import it), `edl` or `srt`.

## Desktop apps: After Effects, Premiere Pro, Blender

A project lives in the browser, but the team can finish it in their own apps. Check
`film_desktop_status` first: it says whether After Effects and Premiere Pro (the Mira panel) and Blender
(the Mira add-on) are connected right now. If an app is off, tell the user to open it, sign in to Mira
and switch the bridge on (mira.mybots.pro/adobe, mira.mybots.pro/blender); do not retry in a loop.

- **Takes into an app.** `film_open_in_app` with up to 12 assetIds and a host (`aeft`, `ppro`, `blender`)
  downloads them on the user's machine. In After Effects and Premiere they go into the Mira bin, or onto
  the open composition or sequence with destination `active`. In Blender an image becomes a reference
  plane and the camera background, a video a Video Sequencer strip and the camera background - the way to
  match a blockout against a take. Any team member's take works, not only the user's own.
- **A cut into Premiere.** `film_edit_open_in_app` rebuilds an Editor cut as a new Premiere Pro sequence
  (host `ppro`, the default): same clips and in/out points, dissolves and dips at the cuts, the sound
  tracks with their levels and fades, the subtitles as a caption track. Host `aeft` makes a composition
  with the clips as layers instead. A long cut takes a few minutes: the panel downloads every file.
- **Back into the bin.** A Blender blockout recording goes into the project with `blender_playblast` and
  `filmProjectId` (a `Blocking` folder from `film_create_folder` keeps it tidy); an After Effects render
  with `adobe_render` and `filmProjectId`; a Premiere sequence export with `adobe_command export_sequence`
  and `film_project_id`. A file from a link goes in with `film_import_url`, a file on disk with
  `create_upload` and `filmProjectId`, the user's own earlier generation with `film_add_generation`.
- **Blockout to take.** Record the blockout into the project, then `generate_video` with `filmProjectId`
  and the recording's url in `referenceVideoUrls` (the `mira-blender-scene` rules for playblast prompts
  apply). The take lands in the bin next to its blockout.

Generations started from the panel or the add-on go into the project only when the user switched it on
there; renders and blockout recordings are free.

## Run the whole studio

Everything the web studio does has a tool. All of them check the user's role in the project.

| Job | Tool |
|---|---|
| Teams | `film_list_workspaces`, `film_manage_workspace`, `film_manage_members` (invites send email: only people the user named), `film_get_usage` |
| Project settings | `film_update_project` (name, slug, cover, move, join link), `film_get_publication`, `film_publish` (public: only when the user asks) |
| Brief in full | `film_get_brief`, then `film_set_brief` with the section's `expectedVersion`; a teammate's save fails your write instead of being lost |
| Bin | `film_search_assets` (filters, paging), `film_get_asset` (with versions), `film_update_assets` (move, mark, like, trash, restore; by `assetIds` or `generationIds`), `film_manage_folder` |
| Cast | `film_get_element`, `film_manage_element` (rename, mark, approve, redraw, import, references) |
| Comments | `film_list_comments`, `film_manage_comment` (add, reply, edit, resolve, reopen) |
| Canvas | `film_get_canvas`, `film_update_canvas` |
| AI Director | `film_director_send` (2 credits a reply; it can start generations), `film_director_history` |
| Release to viewers | `film_release`: `create`, `list`, `get`, `submit` (asks for the catalog, an admin decides), `withdraw`. A project can hold episodes: `create` with `newEpisode` and a `title` adds one and never replaces a film; with several episodes every other call needs `releaseId` from `list`. Only when the user asks; `rightsAttested` only after they confirm the rights |

Put a fresh take into a folder with `film_update_assets`, action `move`, and its `generationId`.

`film_delete` removes things for good and takes two calls: the first changes nothing and returns the
impact and a `confirmToken` for 5 minutes. Show the impact, wait for the user's yes in words, then
call again with the token. To hide a take use `trash`, which can be restored.

`list_brand_assets` returns three kinds of asset with ids:

- **AI Blogger**: the user's recurring character - a person (`kind: human`) or a designed
  character or anthropomorphic animal (`kind: mascot`, which keeps its own render style in every
  scene). Pass `bloggerId` (`avatarId` is the older name of the same parameter and still works).
  The platform injects the canonical shots and an appearance passport (CHARACTER LOCK). Identity
  never changes: face, hair, build, age, marks. Clothes, and the medium of a photoreal person, may
  change; say so in the prompt when they should. A user with none can build one right here:
  `create_blogger_draft` from traits or words, then `save_blogger` (ai-blogger.md); the AI Bloggers
  section of the Mira app does the same. The character sheet (the 2×3 collage) is attached by the
  platform itself; never pass it as a reference URL, a grid in the input turns into a split frame.

rewrite.find:
Seedance screens every photo for real-looking faces before billing. When it refuses one, the
platform registers the refused photos in its private asset library for the length of that one
render, sends the same take again with them as assets, and deletes them as soon as the render
ends - the face stays the one in the photo, and nothing is needed from you: the call simply
takes a little longer. Only AI Blogger, uploaded and library photos go this way; a
stylised request (`style` anime, render3d or pixel, or a drawn medium in the prompt) is redrawn
into one composed start frame instead, because an asset would drag the clip back to photoreal.
